angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 459,162 km at 123.57 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.0925 +/- 0.0236 mas (same row, RUWE 1.25): 123.57 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.66 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Montet et al. 2015, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-17 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...809...25M/abstract): 459,162 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.71 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Montet et al. 2015, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-17 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...809...25M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4320 +/- 56 K from Montet et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-17 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...809...25M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Montet et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-17 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...809...25M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-17.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.650, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
